review_title: impact of GEnAI on OSS Projects review
review_template_title: impact of GEnAI on OSS Projects review
paper_title: [PDF] From Social Coding to Agentic Coding: Productivity and Relational Reconfiguration in Open-Source Communities
logical_feed_name: impact of GEnAI on OSS Projects

values.study_identification: LLM-based multi-agent simulation of OSS developers on GitHub examining effects of coding agents on productivity, interaction modes, and public knowledge retrievability.
values.study_objective: Assess how introducing coding agents changes OSS community productivity, interaction pathways (human–human vs agent-mediated), and the usefulness of public knowledge.
study_population: 1,084 continuously active GitHub developers selected from a public dataset with repository relationships.
Developers spanning diverse languages and roles (contributors, maintainers, mixed).
values.study_period: Historical background: Oct 1, 2014–Jan 21, 2018; Warm-up: Jan 22–Feb 18, 2018; Simulation: Feb 19–Mar 18, 2018; Retrieval benchmark queries: Mar 19–May 19, 2018.
values.genai_definition: Generative coding agents (LLM-based) assisting task understanding, code generation, debugging, testing, revision, and able to execute on a developer’s behalf; primary model DeepSeek V4 with robustness checks using GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.7 (paper also references GLM-5.1/Qwen3 family).
authors_limitations: Fixed developer population and an 8-week window limit analysis of longer-term evolution.
Computational cost limited broader cross-model comparisons; only a few models checked.
Modeling simplification: commits from collaborators are treated as accepted; rejection/rollback/merge conflicts not modeled.
Slight amplification of activity and participation concentration in the simulation relative to real data.
rq1_verification_accountability: Developer agent retains control over task selection and final submission; CA use logged per task.
Commits by collaborators are reviewed; for modeling, all reviewed commits are treated as accepted.
rq1_project_type: Multiple GitHub OSS repositories across diverse programming-language ecosystems.
rq1_project_size_age: Sample requires ≥50 historical commits per developer; mean 50.1 repositories per developer (median 38); observation spans 2014–2018.
rq1_community_structure: Sparse repo-based network: one large component (26% of nodes), many isolated developers (62.5%), mean degree 5.47, nine detected communities; collaboration often localized.
rq1_technical_context: GitHub-based workflows including commits, issue discussion/resolution, repository maintenance; task planning and execution; CA may act on developer’s behalf.
rq1_outcome_construct: Shift from direct human–human interaction to agent-mediated or private loops
Public knowledge coverage and retrievability decline
rq1_outcome_measure: Planned tasks +34.0% (3,151→4,221); completed tasks +39.0% (2,969→4,128); median completion time ~45→20 min.
Knowledge coverage: real-human 81.1% vs CA corpus 22.3%±2.2%; avg retrieval steps 2.63 vs 8.02±0.10; retrieval success 82.3% vs 22.3%±1.4%.
Context breadth ~6.60±0.31 (No-CA) vs 7.05±0.76 (CA); repeated interaction rate ~93.3%±3.7% vs 91.2%±1.6%.
rq1_beneficiary: Developers who are already more active and well connected.
rq1_cost_bearer: Developers who do not adopt or remain unaware of CAs.
Future contributors relying on public records for learning and task support.
rq1_time_horizon: Short term (4-week simulation after a 4-week warm-up).
rq1_supporting_extract: “Planned tasks increase by 34.0%… completed tasks increase by 39.0%… median completion time decreases from ~45 to 20 minutes.” (Fig. 2a–b)
“CA awareness increases from 16.0% to 36.3%, while adoption rises from 6.7% to 26.0%… CA-assisted commits … 25.6% to 65.0%.” (Fig. 3a–b)
“Real-human corpus 81.1% coverage vs CA corpus 22.3%±2.2%; retrieval steps 2.63 vs 8.02±0.10; success 82.3% vs 22.3%±1.4%.”
“Context breadth 6.60±0.31 vs 7.05±0.76; repeated interaction rate 93.3%±3.7% vs 91.2%±1.6%.” (Table 1)
rq2_mechanism: CA availability enables developers to offload coding tasks, increasing throughput and reducing completion time.
Work shifts from public human–human exchange to private human–agent loops and agent-mediated cross-developer execution, reducing visible collaboration.
Reduced public, explanatory records lower knowledge coverage and retrievability for subsequent tasks.
Adoption concentrates among already active, well-connected developers, amplifying participation and production asymmetries.
rq2_antecedent: Introduction/availability of coding agents to developer agents.
Seed adoption by high-activity, multi-language developers; diffusion via shared repositories; task-level decisions to use CA.
rq2_intermediate_process: Developers delegate subtasks to CA, forming private human–agent loops (ASA).
Cross-developer tasks shift from direct HHI to agent-mediated AHI.
Fewer detailed public traces of problem-solving are produced and logged.
rq2_mechanism_outcome: Higher task throughput and faster completion.
Reduced direct interpersonal interaction and visibility of collaboration.
Lower public-knowledge coverage and retrieval success for later tasks.
Participation and production concentrate among already active, well-connected developers.
rq2_moderator: Network position and exposure via shared repositories.
Task characteristics and prior CA experience.
rq2_boundary_condition: Effects observed over a 4-week intervention with a fixed developer population.
Commit reviews assume acceptance; rejections/rollbacks/merge conflicts not modeled.
rq2_alternative_explanation: Lower public-knowledge coverage might reflect private work not logged rather than less knowledge created; nevertheless, a size-matched CA corpus still covers only 22.3% vs 81.1% for real-human records.
rq2_reason_detail: under their settings, they show decreased community pubic exchanges
rq2_supporting_extract: “Completed tasks increase … 1.39x … median completion time decreases … 45 to 20 minutes.”
“Knowledge coverage 81.1% (real) vs 22.3% (CA); retrieval steps 2.63 vs 8.02; success 82.3% vs 22.3%.”
“Adoption rises from 6.7% to 26.0% … CA-assisted commits 25.6%→65.0%; gains concentrated among already active and well connected.”
